quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: A windshield:

options.text: Works as well as a face shield.
Does not fully protect your eyes from wind.
Is required on all motorcycles.
Should be used on windy days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Does not fully protect your eyes from wind.
questions.explanation: A windshield is not a good replacement for goggles or a face shield. Most windshields will not protect your eyes from wind.

questions.question: Which of the following will NOT help reduce your chance of a crash?

options.text: Be visible by wearing bright clothing and using your headlight.
Show your intentions by using turn signals and your brake light.
Look for hazards in your path.
Hope other drivers see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hope other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: To avoid crashes, be visible to other drivers, signal your intentions, and leave space around you. Look for hazards and be ready to react. Do not rely on hoping others see you.

questions.question: When stopping:

options.text: Use the rear brake first.
Use the front brake first.
Use both brakes at the same time.
Use only one brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes together when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: The effects of marijuana can last for:

options.text: No more than 15 minutes.
About one hour.
About two hours.
More than six hours.

questions.correctAnswerText: More than six hours.
questions.explanation: When smoked, marijuana begins to work within minutes and effects last two to four hours. When eaten, it takes over an hour to start working, but effects can last more than six hours.

questions.question: The best source of information about your motorcycle is:

options.text: The previous owner.
The owner's manual.
A library book about motorcycles.
A motorcycle enthusiast.

questions.correctAnswerText: The owner's manual.
questions.explanation: Read the owner's manual before riding your motorcycle for the first time. It has the most important information about your specific motorcycle.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, they should:

options.text: Lean when you lean.
Hold onto the seat.
Sit as far back on the seat as possible.
Never hold onto you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean when you lean.
questions.explanation: Your passenger should lean with you during turns. They should sit forward without crowding you and hold firmly onto your waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: You should increase your distance behind the vehicle ahead when:

options.text: The pavement is dry.
The pavement is wet.
You can see through the vehicle ahead.
The sun is out.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pavement is wet.
questions.explanation: Leave more space when it takes longer to stop. Increase your distance if the road is slippery, if you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or if traffic is heavy.

questions.question: After drinking alcohol, what reduces its effects?

options.text: Exercise
Coffee
Time
Food

questions.correctAnswerText: Time
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate, and nothing speeds this up. Only time will reduce alcohol's effects.

questions.question: When your motorcycle has a sidecar, the passenger should ride:

options.text: On the motorcycle seat.
In the sidecar.
Either on the motorcycle or in the sidecar.
Neither on the motorcycle nor in the sidecar.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the sidecar.
questions.explanation: Your passenger should ride in the sidecar and keep their hands inside at all times.

questions.question: Before riding, your pre-ride check should include everything except:

options.text: Check the tires.
Test the taillight.
Test the headlight.
Check the paint.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the paint.
questions.explanation: Check your tires, oil, fluids, lights, signals, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn before every ride. Do a complete pre-ride check each time.

questions.question: When a rider extends their left arm straight out to the left, what does it mean?

options.text: The rider plans to turn left.
The rider is about to stop.
The rider plans to turn right.
The rider is about to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The rider plans to turn left.
questions.explanation: Riders use hand signals when they do not have mechanical turn signals. A left arm extended straight out means the rider plans to turn left or change lanes to the left.

questions.question: Passing and being passed on a motorcycle is similar to passing in a car. However, what is different?

options.text: A motorcycle is harder to see than a car.
A motorcycle is easier to see than a car.
You should pass on the shoulder instead of the main road.
You must make eye contact with the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: A motorcycle is harder to see than a car.
questions.explanation: Being visible is more important on a motorcycle than in a car. Motorcycles are smaller and can easily hide in a car's blind spot. Other drivers may not notice you even if they are looking.

questions.question: Where is the gear shift lever located?

options.text: In front of the left footrest.
In front of the right footrest.
Behind the left footrest.
Behind the right footrest.

questions.correctAnswerText: In front of the left footrest.
questions.explanation: The gear shift lever is in front of the left footrest and you operate it with your left foot. Push the lever up to shift to a higher gear. Press the lever down to shift to a lower gear.

questions.question: When riding over rough surfaces, what should you do?

options.text: Hold the handgrips loosely to allow movement.
Hold the handgrips firmly to maintain control.
Use a lot of throttle to get over the rough surface.
Ride without a helmet so it does not cover your face.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the handgrips firmly to maintain control.
questions.explanation: When riding over rough ground, grip the handlebars firmly. This keeps your motorcycle under control and moving in the right direction.

questions.question: Experienced riders use "SIPDE" to stay aware of their surroundings. What does the "D" stand for?

options.text: Defer
Decide
Drive
Downshift

questions.correctAnswerText: Decide
questions.explanation: SIPDE is a five-step process used by experienced riders. The letters stand for Scan, Identify, Predict, Decide, and Execute.

questions.question: What do experienced riders do regarding their lane position?

options.text: They change positions in their lane as road conditions change.
They stay in one spot in their lane at all times.
They move side to side in their lane to be more visible.
They only ride on the oily part of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: They change positions in their lane as road conditions change.
questions.explanation: A rider has three lane position choices. An experienced rider picks the safest position based on the road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: What is an advantage of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You can pass danger more quickly.
You have a narrower view of the road so you stay focused.
You have more time to react to other drivers' movements.
You can follow the next vehicle more easily.

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to react to other drivers' movements.
questions.explanation: Keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles gives you a better view of hazards ahead, more time to react to them, and more room to move around them.

questions.question: How does braking in a turn compare to braking on a straight road?

options.text: It is easier than braking on a straightaway.
It is harder than braking on a straightaway.
You should use only the front brake.
You should use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is harder than braking on a straightaway.
questions.explanation: Braking while turning is more difficult than braking on a straight road. You can use both brakes while turning, but you need proper technique and must be very careful.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your chance of a crash?

options.text: Do not use turn signals when changing lanes.
Follow other vehicles closely.
Watch only five feet ahead of your motorcycle.
Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, stay visible to others. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to communicate. Keep space around your motorcycle. Look ahead, behind, and to the sides. Be ready to avoid any unexpected hazard.

questions.question: What is the best formation for group riding?

options.text: Pairs.
A staggered formation.
A single-file line.
A pyramid formation.

questions.correctAnswerText: A staggered formation.
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is usually best for group riding. Switch to a single-file line when turning, riding through curves, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: If a tire goes flat while riding, what should you do?

options.text: Use both brakes and stop as quickly as possible.
Shift your weight toward the tire that is still good.
Brake using the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
Loosen your grip on the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Brake using the good tire and steer to the side of the road.
questions.explanation: If a tire goes flat, hold the handgrips firmly and ease off the throttle. Keep the bike going straight. Brake gently on the tire that is not flat. As you slow down, move to the side of the road and stop.

questions.question: Why is riding alongside a car dangerous?

options.text: It is recommended and safe.
You can be in the driver's blind spot.
It is only a problem on wet roads.
It makes driving easier for the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can be in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding directly next to another vehicle is dangerous. You may end up in the driver's blind spot and cannot see. Also, the vehicle blocks your way to escape.

questions.question: What should your lane position NOT do?

options.text: Help you see and be seen by others.
Help you avoid hazards on the road.
Give you a way to escape danger.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers to share your lane.
questions.explanation: Your lane position should keep you safe in many ways. It should keep you out of blind spots, help you see and be seen, help you avoid road hazards, protect you from wind blasts, and give you an escape route. Your position should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane.

questions.question: What should you do when riding at night?

options.text: Speed up.
Follow closer to the car in front of you.
Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see the road.
Wear tinted glasses.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see the road.
questions.explanation: When riding at night, slow down and increase the distance between you and other vehicles. Use the headlights of cars in front of you to see farther ahead. Be ready to change your lane position as needed.

questions.question: What type of sign is yellow with black letters or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. They tell drivers about road conditions ahead.
